accepted_scope: Linux/x64 and macOS/ARM64 reading-core relocatable candidate: external-argument build, pcfiledir pkg-config unit with the exported compile definitions, removal of private absolute-prefix units, duplicate material removal under a shared permission bit, archive round trip, and installed C, C++ and pkg-config consumers plus nine-format smoke on the relocated prefix and on the extracted archive
scope: Candidate distribution only; SDK freeze, product schema, wire v1 and reading anchors untouched
head_delta_note: Evidence-only commits after the tested SHA change this file and docs/READER-DISTRIBUTION-UNIX.md; no source, test or workflow difference exists between the tested SHA and the final HEAD.

reviewed_delivery.verdict: the delivered build, relocation, dedupe, seal, extraction and consumer runs were real; six concrete packaging/evidence defects were found and repaired on the review branch

repairs: exreader.pc Cflags omitted the compile definitions the installed CMake package exports (EXR_STATIC); a pkg-config consumer therefore got a different compile interface than the package it describes
the public pkg-config unit was only validated as text and never used to build anything
permission bits were recorded but never verified, and byte-identical materials with different executable bits would have been hardlinked into one mode

the sealed manifest's identity, stage_sha256, dedupe_sha256, duplicate saving, root name and member modes were written but never re-derived; the runner identity was unchecked and the protocol artifact's content was never read
check_scope.sh compiled only some package python files, leaving the same-source report tools unchecked
seal.py opened gzip.GzipFile for writing without a mode, emitting a FutureWarning into the protocol log

linux.foreign_pkgconfig: every removed private unit was judged an absolute-prefix defect before removal; a relocatable upstream unit now fails the stage

macos.foreign_pkgconfig: every removed private unit was judged an absolute-prefix defect before removal; a relocatable upstream unit now fails the stage

failures_preserved.reason: stage resolved component target names instead of installed archive names (missing component archive exr_pdf)
C++ consumer brace-initialised the public exr_error record (invalid conversion to exr_status)
audit found six private dependency pkg-config units (libwebp/aom/sharpyuv) with absolute build prefixes before the candidate removed them
audit compared unnormalised pkg-config flags with the relocated prefix and reported false leaks
same-source report keyed the expected artifact map by an unbound name
same-source report wrote the downloaded archive into a missing directory
all jobs green, superseded because the C consumer reported bitmap dimensions after releasing the bitmap (0x0 instead of 720x1040)
the new permission-bit loop in audit.py named its iterator `record`, shadowing the check recorder; both platform jobs failed at `audit before` with TypeError

both platforms and the protocol passed, but the same-source report refused two of its own new bindings: the archive root was compared with the uploaded member path instead of the file name, and gzip.GzipFile emitted a two-line FutureWarning that the new protocol-log guard counts as an unbound line
